mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near its current trough while TRANSIT remains depressed, weekday foot traffic to retail and restaurants will not recover. Over the next four weeks this suppresses RETAIL_REC relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above its prior 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining at or below their current levels for most of the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility after work suppression indicates more time spent at home and less discretionary outings. That shift lowers retail-and-recreation visits within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 7 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its recent 28-day average within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 7 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility deteriorates sharply while GROCERY_PHARM remains less negative, leisure substitution is weak and mixed outing intensity softens. That combination points to a further decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is below -30 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean even though PARKS remains below -30 and GROCERY_PHARM stays above -15 during the prediction window.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals tighter movement conditions or lower access to commercial corridors. That regime shifts retail mobility downward over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 and WORKPLACES falls below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher than its last 28-day mean even after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES cross below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A short-term improvement in GROCERY_PHARM usually reflects more errand-based trips and neighborhood circulation. If that continues for one week, retail-and-recreation mobility should tick up almost immediately.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases week-on-week for one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within the next 7 days after a week-on-week rise in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but PARKS stop falling, households are substituting toward home-centered routines without expanding discretionary outings. That pattern predicts weaker retail mobility over the next two to four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day average while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and PARKS do not recover materially.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained lift in PARKS mobility usually precedes broader leisure demand and nearby shopping trips. If PARKS improves for two weeks, RETAIL_REC should increase over the following month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from its current level and holds for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last 28-day mean within four weeks after PARKS rises and holds above the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stabilize after a prior dip while RESIDENTIAL stops rising, suppressed commute flows are likely bottoming out. That stabilization should keep retail mobility from falling further and can lift it modestly within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stop declining for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 14 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stop falling and RESIDENTIAL no longer increases.
